clue.text: One who has rulers bursting into tears

indicators.note: bursting breaks the words into tears apart so their letters can regroup

explanation.surface: Someone with power over others breaks down crying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rulers' suggests monarchs, but here they are the measuring sticks a stationer sells; 'bursting' rearranges INTO TEARS.
explanation.definitionFit: A stationer's shop stocks writing supplies, rulers among them.

clue.text: Everybody's in this sort of prayer-shawl? No, just the lanky

indicators.note: in places one piece within the jumbled letters
sort of signals a version of this with its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Everyone is wrapped in a prayer shawl, but it turns out only tall people fit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges THIS to TISH, with ALL inside. A tallis is a Jewish prayer shawl, a letter away; the clue says no, the word wanted is the one for the lanky.
explanation.definitionFit: Lanky people are fairly tall, so the word for somewhat tall fits.

clue.text: Long time no see 'this kind of bishop

definitions.text: Long time no see 'this kind of bishop

parts.words: Long time no see 'this kind of bishop
parts.note: a bishop who holds the title of a diocese but has no see to run

explanation.surface: Greeting an old friend who happens to be a bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long time no see' is a greeting, but here a bishop has no see, no diocese of his own: he bears the title only.
explanation.definitionFit: A titular bishop holds the rank of a defunct diocese with no actual jurisdiction.

clue.text: Make excessive net profit?

parts.note: taking too much from the sea with nets, posing as greedy business

explanation.surface: A firm earns too much clear profit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'net profit' is a business term, but here the net is a fishing net.
explanation.definitionFit: Overfishing is taking too many fish so that stocks are depleted.

clue.text: Revolutionary study of blush

parts.note: a red is a revolutionary communist
a den is a private study or room

explanation.surface: A rebel's research into blushing.
explanation.definitionFit: To redden is to turn red in the face, as in a blush.

clue.text: Remember to pass hat round again

definitions.meaning: to gather money a second time

explanation.surface: Someone is reminded to take up a second collection.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the second sense as RE-COLLECT, to collect again.
explanation.definitionFit: To recall to mind, and to collect donations once more, share the spelling.

clue.text: To make merry, try merry-go round endlessly

indicators.note: endlessly means the final letter of the ride's name is dropped

explanation.surface: Advice for having fun: keep riding the roundabout.
explanation.walkthrough: CAROUSEL loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To carouse is to drink and revel noisily.

clue.text: Household linen is put up in it while tea's prepared

definitions.text: Household linen is put up in it

indicators.note: prepared means made ready, so the letters of while tea's are rearranged

explanation.surface: Sheets are hung up while the tea is brewing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' rearranges WHILE TEAS. 'Put up' means offered for sale, not hung on a line.
explanation.definitionFit: A white sale is a shop's sale of bedding and towels.

clue.text: England's first two trees? Nonsense!

indicators.note: first asks for only the opening letter of the word England's

parts.note: the yew is a tree, a common evergreen
the ash is a second tree

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at the claim that two trees are England's finest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two trees' gives two pieces, YEW and ASH, after E from England.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyewash is slang for talk meant to deceive, so rubbish or humbug.

clue.text: Soft soap is smoother

definitions.meaning: to soft-soap someone is to butter them up with praise
more even or level in surface

explanation.surface: A gentler cleanser leaves the skin silkier.
explanation.definitionFit: To soft-soap is to cajole with praise, and a flatter surface is more even than another.

clue.text: He will kick society and kick in Rugby

definitions.meaning: someone who rejects conventional life and leaves it
a drop kick taken to restart play in rugby union

explanation.surface: A rebel turns his back on society and also kicks a ball at school.
explanation.walkthrough: Rugby is a school as well as the game; in rugby union a drop-out is the drop kick that restarts play from the 22-metre line.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who abandons conventional society, and a restarting drop kick in rugby, share the name.

clue.text: Bird found in the picnic hamper?

definitions.meaning: a large thrush that winters in Britain
food eaten out in a meadow, read as two words

explanation.surface: A bird turns up among the sandwiches on a picnic.
explanation.walkthrough: Split it as FIELD FARE: the food you eat in a field.
explanation.definitionFit: The fieldfare is a thrush; split, the name means food for eating out of doors.

clue.text: Chock-full but unusual peer let in

indicators.note: unusual says the letters of peer let appear in an odd order

explanation.surface: A packed house, though an odd lord was admitted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges PEER LET.
explanation.definitionFit: Replete means filled to capacity, especially after eating.

clue.text: Pens once less disturbed

indicators.note: disturbed says the letters of once less are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Animal pens are less troubled than they used to be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' rearranges ONCE LESS. 'Pens' is a verb here, to shut in, not writing tools or the animal enclosures.
explanation.definitionFit: To pen something is to shut it in a confined space.

clue.text: Parts allotted to ploughmen?

parts.note: portions handed out, with the pun that a plough's blade carries the same name

explanation.surface: Ploughmen receive their portions.
explanation.walkthrough: The ploughshare is the cutting blade of a plough, so ploughmen are teasingly given these portions.
explanation.definitionFit: A portion handed out to each person is the same word as a ploughshare's blade.

clue.text: Spinsterhood?

parts.note: an unmarried woman is said to be on the shelf, so her time there is a duration

explanation.surface: The single state.
explanation.walkthrough: An unmarried woman was once said to be 'left on the shelf'; this is a period on the shelf.
explanation.definitionFit: Shelf life is how long a product keeps in store, punned as time spent on the shelf.

clue.text: The language around N E seaport!

indicators.note: around says the letters of N E seaport are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: A lingua franca spoken in a north-eastern port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' rearranges N, E and SEAPORT.
explanation.definitionFit: Esperanto is the artificial international tongue devised by Zamenhof.

clue.text: Hard case gets account for varnish

parts.note: a shell is a hard outer case

explanation.surface: A tough customer buys varnish on credit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard case' suggests a tough person, but it means a shell.
explanation.definitionFit: Shellac is a resin dissolved in alcohol and brushed on wood as a varnish.

clue.text: Liquidator of donkey-team at home

parts.note: a team of two donkeys, an ass and an ass

explanation.surface: A firm's liquidator kept a pair of donkeys at his house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liquidator' suggests a company winder-up, but it means one who liquidates people.
explanation.definitionFit: To liquidate is slang for kill, so a hired killer liquidates.

clue.text: Pen love-letters, perhaps, and wrap them up

indicators.note: the letters of pen love may be taken in another arrangement

explanation.surface: Write love letters and seal them away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letters, perhaps' rearranges PEN LOVE; the surface suggests sealing love-letters in an envelope.
explanation.definitionFit: To envelop is to wrap or enclose completely.

clue.text: Mark of rank from turbulent priest

indicators.note: turbulent means stirred up, so the letters of priest are jumbled

explanation.surface: A rebellious cleric earns a badge of rank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turbulent priest' recalls Henry II's words about Thomas Becket; 'turbulent' rearranges PRIEST.
explanation.definitionFit: A stripe on a uniform sleeve shows a soldier's rank, as with a sergeant's chevrons.

clue.text: Ill-feeling in Franco- Uruguayan bond

indicators.note: in says the letters lie inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Bad blood within an alliance between France and Uruguay.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across fRANCO-URuguayan.
explanation.definitionFit: Rancour is bitter, lasting resentment.

clue.text: Triumph for Pa with liver trouble

indicators.note: liver trouble means the organ is disordered, so the letters of pa and liver are rearranged

explanation.surface: Dad wins despite his liver complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' rearranges PA plus LIVER.
explanation.definitionFit: To prevail is to win or come out on top.

clue.text: Legendary knight, look, in med journals

indicators.note: in says one piece sits inside the name of the journal

parts.note: The Lancet is a well-known British medical journal
lo is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: A famous knight of legend appears in medical periodicals.
explanation.walkthrough: LO goes inside LANCET.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Lancelot is the Arthurian Round Table knight who loved Guinevere.

clue.text: Sorts out books

definitions.meaning: reserves or requests, as a supply is booked

explanation.surface: Someone arranges the volumes on the shelf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'books' is a verb: to place an order for.
explanation.definitionFit: To order is to arrange in sequence, and to place an order is to book or request.

clue.text: Jogger, perhaps, embraces a rest

indicators.note: embraces says the first piece wraps around the single letter

parts.note: a reminder jogs the memory, so it is a jogger

explanation.surface: A runner hugs someone while taking a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jogger' suggests a runner, but it is a memory-jogger, a REMINDER, with A put inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The remainder is whatever is left over, the balance or the others.

clue.text: Lured, sailors say, to these islands…

indicators.note: sailors say signals the seafarers' own pronunciation, which sounds like the clue word

parts.note: enticed; it sounds like the nautical pronunciation of the answer

explanation.surface: Sailors claim they were tempted towards some islands.
explanation.walkthrough: Sailors pronounce it 'LOO-erd', the sound of 'Lured'. The Leeward Islands are in the Caribbean; the ellipsis leads into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The Leeward Islands are a chain in the eastern Caribbean.

clue.text: … south-east coral variety, producing fish

indicators.note: variety means a different form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: SE is the compass abbreviation for south-east

explanation.surface: Coral of a different kind in the south-east gives rise to a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety' rearranges SE plus CORAL together.
explanation.definitionFit: The escolar is a deep-sea mackerel-like fish.

clue.text: Vagrant's blunder

definitions.meaning: someone who drifts from place to place without settled work
a mistake or gaffe, in British slang

explanation.surface: A tramp's slip-up.
explanation.definitionFit: A floater is both a drifter with no fixed home and, in British slang, an embarrassing mistake.

clue.text: Girl has an altered appearance making a pass

indicators.note: an altered appearance is a changed look, so the letters of girl has an are rearranged

explanation.surface: A girl with a new look makes a pass at someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'altered appearance' rearranges GIRL HAS AN. 'Making a pass' suggests flirting, but La is Tibetan for a mountain pass, and Hilton's hidden valley is named as one.
explanation.definitionFit: In Tibetan 'la' means a mountain pass, so the name of Hilton's paradise reads as the Shangri pass.
